parts.title: School Art Competition
parts.transcript: Part 1: a principal and teacher plan the School Art Competition (this year). Junior students: theme animals (1), a drawing, prize zoo tickets (2). Senior students: theme the city (3), a photograph, a travel voucher (4). Submit artwork by 18 May (5) at the library (6). Judge Rebecca Leigh (7), phone 0407 625 4633 (8). Display at Bridge Street Gallery; artworks published in a magazine (9); exhibition followed by a dinner (10).

parts.transcript: Part 3: Gareth and Lorna discuss their survey of third-year music students. Musical background before the degree: could play more than one instrument (21=C) and had performed in public (22=D). Music practice: motivated by fear of failing (23=C) and enjoy the challenge of difficult pieces (24=E). Selecting assessed pieces: like to hear others/recordings of the same pieces (25=A) and play pieces from memory (26=C). Attitudes to performance: solo is difficult but enjoyable (27=B); deciding which pieces is time-consuming (28=E); playing with musicians from a different genre happens infrequently (29=G); playing with musicians on the same instrument is very beneficial (30=A).

parts.title: Gastropods (snails and slugs)
parts.transcript: Part 4: a zoology lecturer on gastropods (snails and slugs). Evolution: minerals in their body fluids resemble those in the sea (31); fossils 500 million years old. Physical features: one muscular foot, radula, shell (snails); most shells coil to the right (32); some have ribs, spines or hair (33). Feeding: mostly rotting plants/fungi/algae; the shield slug eats worms (34). Predators: birds, frogs, flies; snails introduced to Britain as food in the first century by the Romans (35); gastropods develop defences (36) e.g. the glutinous snail makes itself slippery. Habitats: prefer damp/shade; dry conditions are worst (37); biggest variety in old natural habitats e.g. forests (38) and meadowland; the blind snail lives below the ground (39); gastropods indicate the quality of the environment (40).
